{{Short description|American physicist and writer}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=March 2025}}
'''Arthur Guy Zajonc''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|z|eɪ|.|ən|t|s}} {{respell|ZAY|ənts}}; born 11 October 1949 in [[Boston, Massachusetts]]) is an American physicist and the author of several books related to science and mind; one of these is based on dialogues about [[quantum mechanics]] with the [[Dalai Lama]]. Zajonc, professor emeritus at [[Amherst College]] as of 2012,<ref name="On Being with Krista Tippett">{{cite web|url= http://www.onbeing.org/program/arthur-zajonc-michael-mccullough-mind-and-morality-a-dialogue/7316| title= Arthur Zajonc and Michael McCullough| website = On Being with Krista Tippett| access-date= June 17, 2015}}</ref> taught there starting in 1978. He served as the General Secretary of the [[Anthroposophical Society in America]] from 1994 until 2002. From January 2012 to June 2015 he was president of the [[Mind and Life Institute]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mindandlife.org/arthur-zajonc-appointed-as-the-new-president-of-the-mind-life-institute/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120127215759/http://www.mindandlife.org/arthur-zajonc-appointed-as-the-new-president-of-the-mind-life-institute/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 27, 2012 |title=Arthur Zajonc Appointed as the New President of the Mind & Life Institute |date=December 8, 2011 |publisher=Mind & Life Institute |last=O'Brien |first=Chris }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mindandlife.org/with-our-most-sincere-gratitude-to-arthur-zajonc-in-his-transition-from-the-mind-life-presidency/ |title=With our Most Sincere Gratitude to Arthur Zajonc, In His Transition from the Mind & Life Presidency |date=June 25, 2015 |publisher=Mind & Life Institute |last=Jinpa |first=Thupten }}</ref>

==Biography==
Zajonc received a B.S. in engineering physics from the [[University of Michigan]] in 1971. He received an M.S. (1973) and Ph.D. (1976) in physics at the University of Michigan as well. From 1976 to 1978 he was a research associate at the Joint Institute for Laboratory Astrophysics at the [[University of Colorado at Boulder|University of Colorado]] and the [[National Bureau of Standards]], Boulder, Colorado.

Zajonc became an assistant professor of physics at Amherst College in 1978, and was promoted to associate professor in 1984 and full professor in 1991. In 2006 he became an [[Andrew W. Mellon Foundation|Andrew W. Mellon Professor]] at Amherst. He retired from this position in 2011, and is now Andrew W. Mellon Professor Emeritus at Amherst College.<ref>{{cite web|title=Curriculum Vitae |url=http://www.arthurzajonc.org/About.php?subnum=3 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070701105147/http://www.arthurzajonc.org/About.php?subnum=3 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2007-07-01 |work=arthurzajonc.org }} ''Curriculum vitae'' posted on Zajonc's personal website.</ref>

From 1981 to 1982 he was a Visiting associate professor of physics at the [[École Normale Supérieure]] at the [[Laboratoire de Spectroscopie Hertzienne]] in Paris. In 1984 was a Visiting Research Physicist at the [[Max Planck Institute for Quantum Optics]], [[Garching]] ([[Munich]]), Germany with [[H. Walther]]. In 1986 he was a visiting scientist at the Institute for Quantum Optics at [[Leibniz University Hannover]] in Germany. In 1991 he was a visiting scientist at the Department of Physics at the [[University of Rochester]] with L. Mandel. In 1993 he was a [[Fulbright]] Professor at the [[University of Innsbruck]], Austria teaching and doing research on the experimental foundations of [[quantum physics]].

Zajonc was the physics department chairman at Amherst College for three different appointments: 1987–1989, 1998–2000, and 2005–present. Later that same year {{when|date=June 2014}} he was a Scholar-in-Residence at the [[Fetzer Institute]]. He was the Senior Program Director of the Fetzer Institute 1995–1997. He was the director for the Academic Program of the [[Center for Contemplative Mind in Society]] from 2004 to 2009, and served as executive director from 2009 to 2012. In this role, he focused the organization's work on the development and application of [[Contemplation|contemplative practices]] within higher education.

Zajonc held a number of dialogues with the Dalai Lama in 1997 which were published in 2004 under his scientific coordination and editorship as ''Dalai Lama: The New Physics and Cosmology''. He was moderator for the 2003 dialogue with the Dalai Lama at [[MIT]].

==Books==
* {{cite book |last=Zajonc |first=Arthur |title=Catching the Light: The Entwined History of Light and Mind |year=1995 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0195095753}}
* {{cite book |title=The Quantum Challenge: Modern Research on the Foundations of Quantum Mechanics |last1=Greenstein |first1=George |last2=Zajonc |first2=Arthur |isbn=978-0763724702 |publisher=Jones and Bartlett |year=2005 |edition=2nd }} The first edition of this undergraduate text was published in 1997.
* {{cite book |editor1-last=Seamon |editor1-first=David |editor2-last=Zajonc |editor2-first=Arthur |title=Goethe's Way of Science |year=1998 |isbn=978-0791436820 |publisher=State University of New York}}
* {{cite book |editor1-last=Zajonc |editor1-first=Arthur |title=Dalai Lama: The New Physics and Cosmology |year=2004 |isbn=978-0195159943 |publisher=Oxford University Press}} Edited by Zajonc, this book is based on a series of conversations with the Dalai Lama and several prominent physicists about quantum mechanics.
*{{cite book |editor1-last=Harrington |editor1-first=Anne |editor2-last=Zajonc |editor2-first=Arthur |title=The Dalai Lama at MIT |isbn=978-0674027336 |year=2008 |publisher=Harvard University Press}}

* {{cite book |title=The Heart of Higher Education: A Call to Renewal |first1=Parker J. |last1=Palmer |first2=Arthur |last2=Zajonc |first3=Megan |last3=Scribner |isbn=978-0-470-48790-7 |publisher=Jossey-Bass |year=2010}} See one review by Pamela C. Crosby ({{cite web|title=Review of The Heart of Higher Education By Palmer and Zajonc |url=https://characterclearinghouse.fsu.edu/index.php/jon-c-dalton-institute-on-college-student-values/book-reviews/594-review-heart |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402104834/https://characterclearinghouse.fsu.edu/index.php/jon-c-dalton-institute-on-college-student-values/book-reviews/594-review-heart |url-status=dead |archive-date=2015-04-02 |access-date=2012-12-02 }})
